nominal_response.reported_definition: Micellar-fraction carotenoid content divided by undigested-pasta carotenoid content, multiplied by 100
nominal_response.source_locator: Section 2.5.4 equation1; printed p5957 / PDF p6; Section3.2 printed p5960 / PDF p9
nominal_response.distinct_other_outcomes: Equation2 is digesta-normalized micellization; equation3 is digestion recovery. Neither substitutes for equation1.

normalization_adjudication.supporting_evidence: Tables3 and4 label digestion concentrations per100g dry-weight pasta, which could indicate a common initial-pasta basis.
normalization_adjudication.unresolved_evidence: Section2.4.3 freeze-dries aliquots of pasta, digesta and isolated fractions; Section2.5.1 describes extracting weighed samples of each. Supplementary S1/S2 values are labeled mg/100g dry weight. No explicit calculation returning fraction concentrations to total carotenoid amounts, or stating that fraction dry-weight values use initial-pasta mass, was identified.
normalization_adjudication.why_it_matters: A ratio of concentrations per gram of two different dried materials is not necessarily an amount ratio. If both values are already normalized to the same initial-pasta mass, the ratio is compatible. That distinction cannot be resolved confidently from the reported equations and method alone.
normalization_adjudication.information_needed: Confirm whether Filtrate concentrations are per100g of initial dry pasta or per100g of the isolated freeze-dried micellar material. If the latter, provide total fraction dry mass or equivalent back-normalization data.
normalization_adjudication.decision_rule: Established compatible-amount-basis eligibility; independent of response magnitude or fitted performance.

protocol.initial_test_material: Approximately2g freeze-dried cooked and milled pasta; particle size below500um
protocol.source_locator: Sections2.3.2 and2.4.2; printed p5955 / PDF p4; intestinal phase printed p5956 / PDF p5
